intro_md: 🎧 **10 min.** Optional warm-up (2 min): play yesterday's [Friday chat](#2026-11-13-11) once. Then today's sound: **words that join**. Learn it first, then hear it in a new café conversation.

parts.title: Words that join
parts.md:
When a word ends in a **consonant sound** and the next word starts with a **vowel sound**, they **join** – like one long word. You don't hear the gap, so the words seem to disappear.

| You read | You hear | Sounds like |
|---|---|---|
| take it easy | take‿it‿easy | /teɪkɪˈtiːzi/ – "tay-kih-TEE-zee" |
| pick it up | pick‿it‿up | /pɪkɪˈtʌp/ – "pih-kih-TUP" |
| a lot of | a lot‿of | /əˈlɑːtəv/ – "uh-LOT-uv" |
| come in | come‿in | /kʌˈmɪn/ – "kuh-MIN" |
| get up | get‿up | /ɡɛˈtʌp/ – "geh-TUP" |
| used to | used to | /ˈjuːstə/ – "YOOS-tuh" (the *d* disappears!) |

💡 **Why?** The last sound of the first word moves to the start of the next word: *pick‿it‿up* → "pi-ki-tup". Don't look for the gaps – listen for the **music**.

👂 **Listen:** first **slow** (word by word), then **natural** (joined). Tap any line to hear it again, and **whisper along** with the natural one. The last sentence is natural only.

listen.text: Take. It. Easy. It's Sunday.
Take it easy, it's Sunday.
Please. Pick. It. Up. For me.
Please pick it up for me.
We. Have. A. Lot. Of. Time.
We have a lot of time.
Come. In. The. Door. Is. Open.
Come in, the door is open.
Get. Up. It's. Already. Eight.
Get up, it's already eight.
We used to play football here every Sunday.

parts.title: Saturday at Jess's café
parts.md:
![Saturday at the café](data/img/w1/d14-cafe-morning.webp)

Now the joined sounds in a **real conversation**. It's Saturday, 9 am – Nam walks into the café. Try to catch: *come‿in · used to · a lot‿of · pick‿up · take away*.

**Train your ears – the words are hidden at first:**
1. 👂 **Listen without the words.** Just follow. Missed a word? Keep going – the next sentence often explains it.
2. 👂 **Listen again**, still without the words. You'll catch more.
3. 📄 **Show transcript** – listen + read. **Tap any line** you missed to hear just that part again.
4. 👂 **Hide it** and listen one last time.

listen.text: Morning, Nam! Come in, come in. You're up early for a Saturday.
I woke up at six. I'm still not used to getting up in the dark.
That's the Manchester winter. It gets dark at four, and light again at eight.
At home it's always warm. I'm used to wearing a T-shirt all year!
Ha! So what are you doing today? Anything fun?
Not yet. It's my first free weekend, and I don't know the city.
Go to the Saturday market on Station Road. It's amazing.
Really? What do they sell?
Cheap fruit, a lot of vegetables, and there's a man who sells old bikes.
And the dumplings are the best I've ever had. Buy a hot bag for lunch.
That sounds perfect. Can I have a coffee to take away, please?
Sure. Anything to eat with it?
A cheese scone, please. It looks great.
Here you go. That's four pounds twenty.
Thanks. How do I get to Station Road from here?
Take the tram, it's easy. Pick up a map at the tram stop – they're free.
Great, thank you, Jess. See you later!
Have fun! And don't spend all your money on bikes.

parts.title: Quick check + how was it?
parts.md: A few quick questions – tap an answer, you see right away if it's right. Then tell me how much you understood, ask me anything below, and 📤 **Submit**.

options: He wants to go to work
He isn't used to the dark mornings
He is going to the market with Jess

check.answer: He isn't used to the dark mornings
check.why: Nam says: *I'm still not used to getting up in the dark.*

questions.q: What does Jess tell Nam to get at the tram stop?

check.why: Jess says: *Pick up a map at the tram stop – they're free.*
